data.name: Silvano
data.long_meaning: The name Silvano is derived from the Latin word ‘silvanus’ which means ‘from the woods’. In Roman mythology, Silvanus was the god of the woods, forests and fields. In Christian tradition, Saint Silvanus is considered a bishop and martyr in ancient Turkey. He is also known as Silvan and Silvanus of Gaul.

in_latin.name: Silvano
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Silvano derivatum est a latino Silvanus, qui significat 'silvae inhabitans' vel 'densis silvis'. In ecclesia primitiva, nomen Silvanus erat commune inter christianos, qui vitam in silvis et solitudine ducebant.

in_english.meaning: He who belongs to the forest or woods
in_english.long_meaning: The name Silvano originates from the Latin name Silvanus, which means 'he who belongs to the forest' or 'wooded'. It is derived from the Hebrew and Greek roots associated with nature and forests. Silvanus was a Roman god of the forest and fields. The name has been adopted in Christian tradition, symbolizing a connection to nature and the natural world. It signifies someone who is serene, gentle, and protective of the environment.

historical_references.reference: Saint Silvanus was an early Christian martyr whose feast day is celebrated on July 2nd. He is also known as Silvanus of Tarsus. It is believed that he was a disciple of the Apostle Paul and was martyred in Greece during the reign of Nero in AD 64.

Another Saint Silvanus, also known as Silvanus of Montenegro, was born in the 14th century and was a Serbian Orthodox monk and hermit. He is said to have lived in solitude in the Montenegrin mountains for over 50 years. Saint Silvanus is revered as a protector of the Montenegrin people and is the patron saint of Montenegro.
